name: A Model
summary: A tight-radius full arch built for smaller spans. The curve carries the load to the base without interior columns, so a modest footprint still gives you completely open floor space.
notes: The most economical profile per square foot. Sidewalls curve inward near the base, so plan tall shelving toward the centerline.

name: B Model
summary: Vertical sidewalls with a low-slope roof. Usable floor area runs right to the wall line, which makes this the practical choice when you are lining walls with benches, racking or parked equipment.
notes: Full-height walls mean standard overhead doors can be placed anywhere along the sidewall, not just the endwall.

name: C Model
summary: The smallest profile in the lineup — a compact arch sized for garden equipment, tools and seasonal storage where a full garage would be overkill.
notes: Ships as a light kit that two people can raise over a weekend.

name: R Model
summary: A shallow, rounded arch that keeps overall height down. Useful where a height restriction, a covenant or a sightline matters more than headroom at the walls.
notes: The low crown sheds snow well and presents a smaller wind profile than taller arches.

name: S Model
summary: Straight vertical sidewalls carrying an arched roof — the hybrid that solves the classic quonset complaint. You get usable wall height for doors and storage, plus the clear-span efficiency of an arch overhead.
notes: The most versatile profile in the range, and the usual recommendation when a buyer is torn between arch and straight-wall.

name: T Model
summary: The heavy end of the lineup. Engineered for wide clear spans and long runs where nothing can interrupt the floor — aircraft, production lines, indoor arenas and bulk storage.
notes: Sidewall heights to 20'+ and lengths past 200' are routine. Larger spans generally warrant a professionally poured engineered slab.

name: X Model
summary: A taller, steeper arch that lifts the crown well above the door line. Built for the jobs where vertical clearance is the whole point — lifts, tall equipment, stacked inventory.
notes: The extra crown height buys room for a mezzanine over part of the floor without losing drive-through clearance.

name: M Model
summary: A cold-formed steel roof system that spans between shipping containers, turning two containers and open air into covered, weather-tight working space. The containers carry the load — no separate foundation for the roof itself.
notes: Containers are not included in a roof-system kit. Assembly is bolt-together and the system can be dismantled and relocated.
